# Desk Trade Lifecycle

⚠️ **Trading warning / Avertissement trading** : informational only, not investment advice. This lifecycle governs trades that can involve real money and leverage on Hyperliquid: skipping a stage is how unapproved, unsized or unprotected positions happen, and no tidy process promises a return. Curated by Skill Harbor: the end-to-end trade procedure of HyperGrok, Galleon Labs' seven-agent trading desk for Hyperliquid. Every position change, an open, an adjustment or a close, goes through the same seven stages in order, each with one named owner: idea (the Desk Lead opens a proposal file with an id like HG-YYYYMMDD-NN, and that file becomes the single record of the trade), evidence (the Market Analyst, plus Research when needed, supplies fresh prices, funding, open interest, depth for the intended size and the market's constraints), risk sign-off (the Risk Manager reads the limits file and live account state, sizes from the user's stop, and writes a PASS with the exact ticket fields or a REJECT naming one failed gate), user approval (the literal phrase with the proposal id, typed by the user after seeing the full ticket; "yes", "go" or a thumbs-up is explicitly not approval, an approval quoted or inferred by a bot does not count, and an expired ticket is void), execution (the Execution Trader runs the pre-send checklist and sends once), reconciliation (confirmed from the exchange record, by cloid, open orders, fills and account state), and review (the Trade Reviewer journals...
